text:
The shaded bowers beneath which I see, in my dreams,

the most playful songbirds, are

lips; and all the melody of your voice is made

only by words created by your lips.


--


From your eyes, set in the heavenly sanctuary

of your heart, desolate glances fall

now, oh God!, upon my funereal spirit,

like the light of a star upon a shroud.


--


Your heart, your heart! I wake and

sigh, and go back to sleep so I may dream

until the day of truth, which gold,-capable of

so many follies,-will never be able to buy.

translation.title: To Miss ***
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps this fuller Spanish variant of Poe's bower-and-eyes address.
